children: unveiled a new enterprise-security framework Wednesday, but its shares traded down 8.35% at $56.66 at 12:10 p.m. ET Thursday. The pitch is straightforward: give businesses tighter control over sensitive AI workloads. The commercial test is tougher. Those controls need to help turn enterprise interest into paying customers.

The framework combines six protections, including customer-controlled encryption keys, customer authorization for provider access and checks on the infrastructure running workloads. Some capabilities remain on the roadmap. CoreWeave plans to extend confidential computing across processors, graphics chips and their interconnections, with Rubin NVL8 systems expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. That makes deployment progress a key detail to watch. A security announcement opens the conversation; available products give customers something to buy.

The GuruFocus snapshot shows a GF Score of just 8/100 and a loss-making business, underscoring how much CoreWeave still has to prove financially. Its $31.25 billion market capitalization sits alongside a substantially larger $76.44 billion enterprise value. Better security could help attract proprietary enterprise workloads, but it does not establish their profitability. Investors need evidence that new contracts produce enough cash to support the infrastructure behind them.

title: CoreWeave Stocks Drop 8.35% Despite Enterprise AI Security Expansion
